summary: Your preliminary ZYZZsat design is strong and technically sound: the launch trade, J2 sun-synchronous orbit, STK access work, data budget and drag-sail EOL are well evidenced and numerically consistent. The main gaps are the missing link, power and mass budgets and the unexamined optics volume. These are largely acknowledged. Marks are unchanged; the feedback below shows how to move each criterion toward the top of its band.
next_steps: Close the missing engineering budgets in Sections 2.4 and 2.5: add an X-band link budget (antenna gain, EIRP, C/N0, modulation) to substantiate 50 Mbit/s to the 12 m dish, and add mass and power budgets (solar array, battery for the 34 min eclipse) to show the 50 kg bus closes.

Address the optics feasibility flagged in Table 1 and Section 2.3: calculate the focal length implied by 5 m GSD at 600 km and explain how the folded optics fit within the 0.6 m box, or revise the GSD/aperture assumption.

Strengthen the orbit and coverage evidence: apply a 10° elevation constraint directly in STK rather than correcting 0° access by hand, and refine the revisit estimate in Table 3 for latitude-dependent ground-track spacing and roll-access geometry.

criteria.C1: You address all four required elements in Section 1 with specific detail: mission, need, single-spacecraft rationale and AIMS/GBRMPA users. The bleaching-monitoring and resolution arguments are well made. To reach the top of Accomplished, replace the National Geographic source with peer-reviewed literature and add a little more customer-requirement detail.
criteria.C2: Section 2 is comprehensive: launch trade and fallback, full orbital elements with a verified J2 SSO calculation, manoeuvre rationale, STK access, data budget, duration and drag-sail EOL. To reach the top band, close the link, power and mass budgets and examine the optics focal-length/volume issue; these are the remaining unsupported requirements.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion is specific and quantitative, drawing on revisit, pass frequency, margin and decay lifetime, and it honestly lists limitations and next steps. To secure the highest level, map each conclusion explicitly back to the mission-design requirements and state the quantified margin or evidence for each.
criteria.C4: The report has a clear engineering structure, a concise abstract, numbered sections, captioned figures/tables with sources, consistent IEEE-style citations and an STK appendix. To reach the top of Accomplished, add page numbers to the contents, replace weak web references, support the reef-area claim, and check formatting consistency throughout.
